capabilities: Render collapsed lookback rows for daily-note sections from prior years, months, or custom intervals
Lazy-load section content per row on expand or hover instead of at note open
Configure intervals, cutoffs, headings, and styles via code-block keys and settings
Insert, refresh, and expand/collapse lookback blocks through commands
Style rows with four presets and theme-derived accent colors
extras: Not yet in the community catalog; installation requires BRAT or manually copying release files into the plugins folder. README states the plugin makes zero network requests and renders lookback content read-only.
intentEvidence: Native embeds load and render the entire source file at every note open.
motivation: The author found that the standard template-script recipe of stamping native embeds taxed note-opening performance forever, and no existing plugin offered lazy lookbacks, so they built one.
problem: Native embeds of past daily-note sections re-parse whole source files on every note open, so journals with years of template-stamped embeds open slowly, worst on mobile.

relations.evidence: The plugin reads your Daily Notes (or Periodic Notes) folder and date format automatically
install with BRAT pointed at this repo

summary: Code-block plugin that renders collapsed lookback rows of daily-note sections from past years, months, or custom intervals, loading content only on expand.
